1.explanation:
The root of the issue is that TableContainer renders the title and description nodes without any id attributes, so when a consumer passes aria-labelledby or aria-describedby on the and points to the container’s id, assistive technologies cannot find individual ids for the title/description elements to announce. To fix this, TableContainer (and/or the DataTable.getTableContainerProps helper) must generate or accept explicit id props for the title and description elements—e.g. titleId and descriptionId—and attach them to the

and

respectively. The DataTable.getTableContainerProps function should supply a base id for the container and derive title- and description-specific ids so that aria-labelledby and aria-describedby on the

can correctly reference the visible label and description.
1.bug_scenario:
The user renders a DataTable with a TableContainer supplying a title and description, and attempts to label the underlying by passing aria-labelledby referencing the TableContainer’s id. Because the

title and

description inside TableContainer do not themselves receive id attributes, the screen reader cannot resolve any labelledby references and instead falls back to reading table contents as the label. The provided screenshots show JAWS reading concatenated header and cell text rather than the visible title+description.

Because neither of those prop getters nor the TableContainer component inject the proper IDs, assistive technology cannot locate the correct label and description elements, leading to the observed screen-reader fallback behavior.
